quickAnswer: Antalya Archaeology Museum ranks alongside Istanbul's Archaeological Museums and Ankara's Museum of Anatolian Civilizations for its unmatched Roman sculpture from Perge. Important 2026 update: the museum closed on 16 July 2025 and was demolished in September 2025 for seismic rebuilding, remaining closed through late 2026 while its 100,000 artifacts sit in storage.

body.text: What Roman marble statues from Perge fill the Hall of the Gods?

The Hall of the Gods houses second-century CE Roman marble statues excavated from nearby Perge, including Zeus, Aphrodite, Tyche, Nemesis, Artemis, and the reunited Weary Herakles. Sculpted from fine Anatolian marble, these larger-than-life figures earned the museum the 1988 Council of Europe Museum Prize and anchor its top-three national reputation.

No other regional museum in Türkiye matches this density of intact imperial statuary. Alongside the Olympian deities stand the Emperors' Hall portraits—Trajan, Hadrian, Septimius Severus, and Perge's celebrated female civic benefactor Plancia Magna—plus the [Weary Herakles](https://www.worldhistory.org/image/13609/weary-hercules-statue-from-perge/), whose upper torso was repatriated from Boston's Museum of Fine Arts in 2011 to rejoin the legs excavated in Perge in 1980. Following a seismic risk review, the Ministry of Culture and Tourism [closed the 1972 building in July 2025](https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/100-000-artifacts-from-antalya-museum-relocated-ahead-of-demolition-213580), relocated roughly 100,000 artifacts into secure storage, and demolished the structure in September 2025 to build a new [20,000-square-meter Perge-inspired museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antalya_Museum) on the same Konyaaltı Caddesi site.
How long should you budget (2 hours) and how do you reach it via the historic tram from Kaleiçi?

Once the rebuilt galleries reopen, budget two full hours to move comfortably through the Perge sculpture halls, Roman sarcophagi, and Lycian coin rooms without rushing. From Kaleiçi, the historic T2 Nostalgia Tram runs roughly 15 to 17 minutes from Üç Kapılar (Hadrian's Gate) or Kalekapısı directly to Müze Station.

Because both the museum and transit lines have seen 2026 disruptions, double-check live operating status before setting out. The [T2 Nostalgia Tram](https://turkeytravelplanner.com/antalya-nostalgic-tramway/) traditionally links Zerdalilik, Hadrian's Gate, Kalekapısı, and Müze along the cliffs above Konyaaltı, though [Urban Transport Magazine reported a temporary T2 suspension in August 2026](https://www.urban-transport-magazine.com/en/antalya-historic-tramway-service-suspended-for-the-time-being/). When T2 is out of service, take the modern T3 tram to Müze, catch municipal bus 600, or ride a 5-to-10-minute taxi covering the 3 km distance from Kaleiçi.

body.text: Yes. As a Ministry of Culture and Tourism state museum, Antalya Archaeology Museum is covered by both MuseumPass Türkiye (€165 in 2026, valid 15 days nationwide) and MuseumPass The Mediterranean (€90, valid 7 days across Antalya, Denizli, Mersin, and Adana) once it reopens to the public.

Verify pass math before buying, especially while Antalya's flagship indoor museum remains under reconstruction. According to the [official Ministry e-ticket portal](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-ekle?catalogNo=WEB-PMK01-87-009), standalone 2026 tickets include Aspendos (€15), Patara (€15), Myra (€13), Phaselis (€10), Olympos (€10), and Hierapolis-Pamukkale (€30). Note that [MuseumPass The Mediterranean](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-MSP01-25-009) covers one entry per included site during standard daytime hours and excludes Night Museum sessions and Pamukkale's Antique Pool.
Why is visiting on a hot summer afternoon ideal?

Visiting between 13:00 and 16:30 in July or August trades 36°C coastal heat for climate-controlled marble galleries, letting you schedule open-air ruins like Perge or Aspendos at 08:00. Afternoon visits also finish right as sea breezes cool nearby Konyaaltı Beach and Kaleiçi's cliffside promenades.
Until the new museum doors open, keep this same heat-smart structure using open indoor alternatives.

faq.q: Is the Antalya Archaeology Museum open in 2026?
faq.a: No. The museum closed on 16 July 2025 and was demolished in September 2025 due to earthquake safety concerns. It remained closed for reconstruction into late 2026; always verify its live status on muze.gov.tr before visiting.

faq.q: What happened to the Perge statues during the demolition?
faq.a: Nearly 100,000 artifacts, including the Hall of the Gods marble statues and the Weary Herakles, were packed by conservation teams and moved into secure storage while the new building is constructed on the same site.

faq.q: How much does MuseumPass Türkiye cost in 2026?
faq.a: On the official Ministry of Culture and Tourism portal (muze.gov.tr), MuseumPass Türkiye costs €165 for foreign visitors, while the 7-day MuseumPass The Mediterranean costs €90.

faq.q: Is the T2 Nostalgia Tram running to the museum stop in 2026?
faq.a: Service on Antalya's historic T2 tram was temporarily suspended in August 2026. Travelers heading to Konyaaltı or the museum district can use the modern T3 tram, municipal bus 600, or a short taxi from Kaleiçi.

faq.q: What is the best alternative while Antalya Archaeology Museum is closed?
faq.a: Pair a morning visit to Perge Ancient City (where the museum's statues originally stood) with Kaleiçi's Antalya Ethnographic Museum or a coastal drive to the renovated Museum of Lycian Civilisations in Demre.

faq.q: Why is Antalya Archaeology Museum considered one of Türkiye's top three?
faq.a: Its unmatched concentration of intact Roman marble sculptures from Perge, Imperial portraits, ornate sarcophagi, and the repatriated Weary Herakles earned it the 1988 Council of Europe Museum Prize.
